thread:
maya: Quick check — trying to finalize onboarding for zeno-14b. Do we have the canonical registry path for weights (and a mirror) or should I point to HF?

jordan: We have a staged copy in the registry but not mirrored to public HF yet. Registry path is s3://redwood-registry/models/zeno-14b/2026-03-15/weights.tar.zst

sam: Heads-up: the manifest used for this model is v2 (fields: filename, sha256, size, quantization). Make sure the serving-validator accepts v2. I just saw a validation error on my local run.

maya: Great — can someone paste the sha256 so I can precompute cache keys?

eli: sha256: 3b8f9d2a7c4e9a1b2c4d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7

sam: Also note: the registry copy has a small tokenizer mapping tweak compared to HF — special tokens mapping changed (BOS/EOS ids). Serving runtime expects eos_id=2; HF bundle uses eos_id=50256.

maya: Oof — that will break padding/truncation test. Is there a config diff we can apply automatically?

jordan: We can override tokenizer ids at load time via model config in the registry manifest. Example patch we use:

```json
{"tokenizer_overrides": {"bos_token_id": 1, "eos_token_id": 2}}
```

sam: If you're going to patch, please also update max_seq_length in the runtime config. The model's config.json claims 8192 but the weights were exported for 4096 — mismatch causes KV cache issues.

maya: Whoa — that's probably why I hit weird pasting truncation in smoke tests. Can someone confirm actual supported seq len?

eli: Confirmed: weights were distilled/exported at 4096. I can rebuild a small manifest entry with corrected config and checksum.

maya: Perfect. Two more quick things: do we have presign policy for the registry reads? If I link to the s3 path in the onboarding doc the link needs a TTL for customers.

jordan: Registry serves internal VPC reads without presign for Dedicated, but for external QA we generate presigned URLs with a 12h TTL via the artifact service. Use the artifact-service endpoint: https://artifact.redwood.internal/presign?path=models/zeno-14b/2026-03-15/weights.tar.zst

sam: Note for ops: please don't use short TTLs for heavy downloads — rehydration jobs will restart and thrash cache. 12h is fine.

maya: Thanks. Eli, when you update manifest can you also publish a minimal diff so I can rerun the validator and post a brief PR?

eli: Yep — will push manifest update + new sha256 and set tokenizer_overrides + max_seq_length=4096. Pushing in ~15m.

build-bot: CI: model-validator job queued for zeno-14b (job id: mv-2781).

maya: Cool. After the manifest update I will run the serving smoke (local with small batch) and ping for a canary rollout. If it passes, we'll mirror to HF and update the public catalog.

sam: One last oddball — tokenizer uses bpe-v2 merges file with windows line endings in the HF bundle. That caused our tokenizer loader to treat one token as two. Might want to normalize when we mirror.

maya: Good catch. If Eli can normalize merges and update manifest entries, I'll schedule the mirror and add a short note to the onboarding checklist about normalizing merges + verifying bos/eos.

eli: On it. I'll include a small shell snippet in the manifest notes for future:

```bash
# normalize merges file
tr -d '\r' < merges.txt > merges.normalized.txt
# update manifest and recompute sha
sha256sum weights.tar.zst | awk '{print $1}'
```

maya: Perfect. Thanks all :thumbsup:

jordan: Ping me if the validator complains about quantization profile mismatch — we had a similar issue last week where quantization field was unset and runtime picked an inefficient kernel.

maya: Will do. Leaving this thread open until the manifest is updated and CI passes.

eli: Manifest + normalized merges pushed. New sha256: a7c6b5d4e3f20198b7c6d5e4f3a2b1c0d9e8f7a6

build-bot: CI: model-validator mv-2781 started.

maya: Thanks — running local smoke now. Will post results in ~10m.
